'''Itsukahara Kofun''' (五塚原古墳) is a [[kofun]] located in [[Muko City]], {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|en|Kyoto Prefecture|qid=Q120730|lt=Kyoto Prefecture}}, Terado Town, Shibayama. It is a [[Keyhole-shaped Kofun|keyhole-shaped tumulus]] and part of the Muko Hills Kofun Cluster. It has been Historic site a {{ill|Historic site|en|Historic site|qid=Q1081138|lt=Historic site}} of Japan (included in the "Otokuni Kofun Cluster").

This is one of the oldest large keyhole-shaped kofun from the mid-to-late {{ill|3rd century|en|3rd century|qid=Q8101|lt=3rd century}}, representing the earliest period of the [[Kofun period]].<ref name="2015th year 12月" />

Itsukahara Kofun is located on a ridge in the southern part of the Muko Hills, at the southwestern edge of the [[Kyoto Basin]]. Several other large keyhole-shaped kofun are also distributed in the Muko Hills, collectively referred to as the "Muko Hills Kofun Cluster."<ref name="第5次調査 現地説明会資料|2014">{{Sfn|2014 Survey Materials}}</ref> Although part of the northwest side of the circular rear section has been leveled for residential development, the overall mound remains well-preserved.<ref name="京都府埋蔵文化財情報 第64号|1997">{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Report No. 64|1997|pp=35-37}}</ref> Several excavations have been conducted to date.

The mound features a southward-facing front section with a "paddle" type typical of early keyhole-shaped kofun.<ref name="2015th year 12月">[https://www.kyoto-np.co.jp/sightseeing/article/20151216000139 "Rear section types a perfect circle; Could this be the prototype of a king's tomb?" Kyoto Shimbun, December 16, 2015.]</ref> The mound is built in three tiers in the rear circular section and two tiers in the front section, primarily from packed soil.<ref name="2015th year 12月" /><ref name="第3次調査 現地説明会資料|2013">{{Sfn|2013 Survey Materials}}</ref> The surface of the mound contains remnants of stone lining, but no haniwa (clay figures) have been found.<ref name="第8次調査 現地説明会資料|2016">{{Sfn|2016 Survey Materials}}</ref> The burial chamber is a vertical stone chamber located at the top of the circular rear section.<ref name="2019th year 9月">[https://www.kyoto-np.co.jp/sightseeing/article/20190906000188 "Stone chamber made only of natural stones uncovered for the first time in an early kofun in Muko, Kyoto," Kyoto Shimbun, September 7, 2019.]</ref> Additionally, a haniwa coffin has been discovered as a peripheral burial near the west slope of the circular rear section.<ref name="2016th year 10月">[https://www.kyoto-np.co.jp/sightseeing/article/20161013000130 "Was it a chief's fourth-generation relative? Haniwa coffin found at Itsukahara Kofun," Kyoto Shimbun, October 13, 2016.]</ref>

The construction period is estimated to be the mid-to-late {{ill|3rd century|en|3rd century|qid=Q8101|lt=3rd century}}, making it the oldest in the Muko Hills cluster of chief's tombs.<ref name="南2013rd year " /> The "slope-shaped flat surface" of the mound is an old design shared with the {{ill|Hashihaka Kofun|en|Hashihaka Kofun|qid=Q11603420|lt=Hashihaka Kofun}} in {{ill|Sakurai, Nara|en|Sakurai, Nara|qid=Q127026|lt=Sakurai, Nara}} (believed by some to be Queen [[Himiko]]'s tomb).<ref name="2015th year 12月" />

The site was Historic site as a {{ill|Historic site|en|Historic site|qid=Q1081138|lt=Historic site}} of Japan in {{ill|2016|en|2016|qid=Q25245|lt=2016}}.<ref name="国指定">Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science, and Technology Notification No. 31, March 1, 2016.</ref>

== Excavation History ==
* {{ill|1967|en|1967|qid=Q2648|lt=1967}}-{{ill|1968|en|1968|qid=Q2644|lt=1968}}: Survey conducted by Kyoto Prefectural Board of Education.<ref name="京都府埋蔵文化財情報 第64号|1997">{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Report No. 64|1997|pp=35-37}}</ref>
* 1968: Electric survey conducted by Tezukayama University.<ref name="京都府埋蔵文化財情報 第64号|1997">{{Sfn|Kyoto Archaeological Report No. 64|1997|pp=35-37}}</ref>
* {{ill|1977|en|1977|qid=Q2481|lt=1977}}: Survey conducted by Kyoto University Archaeology Laboratory.<ref name="第3次調査 現地説明会資料|2013">{{Sfn|2013 Survey Materials}}</ref>
* {{ill|2000|en|2000|qid=Q1985|lt=2000}}-{{ill|2001|en|2001|qid=Q1988|lt=2001}}: First and second excavations conducted by Ritsumeikan University.<ref name="第3次調査 現地説明会資料|2013">{{Sfn|2013 Survey Materials}}</ref>
* {{ill|2013|en|2013|qid=Q1998|lt=2013}}: Third and fourth excavations conducted by Muko City designation1 Center and Ritsumeikan University.<ref name="第3次調査 現地説明会資料|2013">{{Sfn|2013 Survey Materials}}</ref>
* {{ill|2014|en|2014|qid=Q1999|lt=2014}}: Fifth and sixth excavations conducted by Ritsumeikan University.<ref name="第6次調査 現地説明会資料|2014">{{Sfn|2014 Survey Materials}}</ref>
* {{ill|2015|en|2015|qid=Q2002|lt=2015}}: Seventh excavation conducted by Muko City designation1 Center.<ref name="第7次調査 現地説明会資料|2015">{{Sfn|2015 Survey Materials}}</ref>
* {{ill|2016|en|2016|qid=Q25245|lt=2016}}: Designated as a {{ill|Historic site|en|Historic site|qid=Q1081138|lt=Historic site}} of Japan. Eighth excavation conducted.<ref name="第8次調査 現地説明会資料|2016">{{Sfn|2016 Survey Materials}}</ref>
* {{ill|2017|en|2017|qid=Q25290|lt=2017}}: Ninth excavation conducted by Muko City designation1 Center.<ref name="第9次調査 現地説明会資料|2017">{{Sfn|2017 Survey Materials}}</ref>
* {{ill|2018|en|2018|qid=Q25291|lt=2018}}: Tenth excavation conducted.<ref name="2019th year 9月">[https://www.kyoto-np.co.jp/sightseeing/article/20190906000188 "Stone chamber made only of natural stones uncovered for the first time in an early kofun in Muko, Kyoto," Kyoto Shimbun, September 7, 2019.]</ref>

== Mound area ==
The reconstructed area of the mound are as follows:<ref name="第8次調査 現地説明会資料|2016">{{Sfn|2016 Survey Materials}}</ref>
* Mound length: 91.2 m
* Rear circular section:
** Diameter: 55 m
** Height: 8.7 m
** burial: Three tiers
* Front section:
** Length: 40.5 m
** Width: 33 m
** Height: 4.0 m
** burial: Two tiers
* Neck section:
** Width: 15 m
** Height: 2.1 m
The design is noted for similarities with the {{ill|Higaida Ōtsuka Kofun|en|Higashida Ōtsuka Kofun|qid=Q11528075|lt=Higaida Ōtsuka Kofun}} in Sakurai, Nara.<ref name="第7次調査 現地説明会資料|2015">{{Sfn|2015 Survey Materials}}</ref>

== burial ==
The burial facility is a vertical stone chamber at the top of the rear circular section.<ref name="2019th year 9月">[https://www.kyoto-np.co.jp/sightseeing/article/20190906000188 "Stone chamber made only of natural stones uncovered for the first time in an early kofun in Muko, Kyoto," Kyoto Shimbun, September 7, 2019.]</ref>

== Relics ==
The only confirmed relic is the haniwa coffin found near the west slope of the rear circular section.<ref name="第8次調査 現地説明会資料|2016">{{Sfn|2016 Survey Materials}}</ref>

== Historic site ==
=== National Historic site ===
* Itsukahara Kofun: Designated as part of the "Otokuni Kofun Cluster" in {{ill|2016|en|2016|qid=Q25245|lt=2016}}.<ref name="国指定">Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science, and Technology Notification No. 31, March 1, 2016.</ref>
